read.passage: Faisal is fifteen, and he has been building small robots since he was ten. His first robot was made from old toy cars and a broken phone. "It could only move forward," he laughs. For the last two years, he has been working on a robot that helps farmers in Al-Qassim. It is designed to check the soil and tell farmers when their palm trees need water. The robot was tested on his uncle's farm last spring, and it was chosen as one of the best projects at a national science fair. "If I had more money, I'd build ten more," Faisal says. "I wish every farmer could use one. It would save so much water."

qs.q: How long has Faisal been building robots?

read2.passage: The Arabian leopard is one of the rarest big cats in the world. Fewer than two hundred are thought to live in the wild. For years, they have been losing their homes as towns have grown. In Saudi Arabia, a programme was started to protect them. Several leopard cubs have been born at a centre in Taif, and scientists hope that one day some of them can be returned to the mountains of AlUla. 'If people understood how special these animals are, they would protect them,' says one of the scientists. Visitors can't see the leopards at the centre, but the programme has been sharing videos online so that people can follow the cubs as they grow.

qs.q: Why have the leopards been losing their homes?
